# Futuristic themes for DeepSeek Harness Desktop

Three cinematic sci-fi themes for **DeepSeek Harness**, built from the three original design
briefs

and the concept rendering in `docs/design-briefs/`, and delivered
as one installable plugin for Deep
Seek Harness Desktop.
| Nostromo Amber | Omni-tool | Renaissance Steel |

`Settings → General → Futuristic themes` — the row the plugin adds (shown with Nostromo Amber
active
), and the same theme applied to the real app:
## What is here
| Path | What it is |
| `dsh-futuristic-themes/` | the plugin: three registered themes, one Appearance row, optional decor

ative layer |
| `docs/THEME-CONTRACT.md` | authoring contract: palette roles, token derivation, effe

cts rules, preview loop |
| `docs/INSTALL.md` | Desktop install (plugin manager or manual profile ed

it) and rollback |
| `docs/qa/` | independent audit harness output + end-to-end verification report

and screenshots |

ler |
| `docs/design-briefs/` | the original design briefs for each theme (Russian, verbatim) + the
concept rendering, with English digests |
## The three themes

### Nostromo Amber — retro CRT terminal
*Original brief: `docs/design-briefs/Nostromo-Amber.md`*
Alm

ost-black warm metal (`#0B0804`), amber phosphor (`#FFB000` accents, `#FFD98A` text),
1 px amber bez

els, monospace type, restrained CRT layer (fine scanlines, phosphor halo, heavy
vignette). Hot `#FF4

A1C` warnings and `#7FBF3F` OK states. No glow on long-form text; long
sessions stay readable.

### Omni-tool — holographic HUD
*Original brief: `docs/design-briefs/Omni-tool.md`*
Dark blue glass

(`#0A0D12`, four glass surface steps), orange action accent (`#FF9A1F`),
cold cyan secondary signals

(`#3FD0FF` reserved for informational states), warm `#F2E3C9`
text, thin warm frames. Decorative la

yer: top-fading cyan/warm projection grid + corner glows.
Orange commands actions; cyan never compet

ding cyan/warm projection grid + corner glows.
Orange commands actions; cyan never competes with it.

### Renaissance Steel — cold industrial console
*Original brief: `docs/design-briefs/Renaissance-Ste

el.md`*
Flat steel surfaces (`#07090C` / `#0E1318`), 1 px blue-grey frames (`#26323D`), `#5FB4E6`
ac

cent, `#BCD0E0` text, `#5FD3B0` success, `#E2553F` warning. Almost no glow: a faint overhead
light,
a hairline steel bezel and a soft corner vignette — the calmest theme of the three.

All three replace the complete semantic `--dsw-*` token set (127 tokens each) and switch the
interfa

ce to a monospace stack; the decorative layer can be disabled in one click and respects
`prefers-red
uced-motion`. They are dark-only by design.
## How it works

- The plugin registers three theme definitions through the host's official third-party theme
extensi

on point (`ctx.theme.register`) and contributes one `settings.general.item` row.
- A compact palette

(15 roles + optional per-token overrides) is expanded by
`scripts/lib/derive.mjs` into the full tok

en
set, so every theme is complete by construction; the build fails on missing required tokens
and w

arns on contrast regressions.
- `ui-theme.preference` only accepts `light|dark|system`, so a theme i

d is never written there
(that would crash the next boot with `theme registry lost`). The selected t

heme lives in
`localStorage` and is re-applied after the host settings document loads; the durable
p

reference stays `dark`, which also makes the first paint already dark.
- Choosing the host's built-i

n Light/Dark/System appearance exits the theme deliberately and
does not resurrect it on reload.
- N

othing host-side is registered: no services, routes, tools or settings namespaces. The
browser half

imports only `react` + the host services it declares. Decorations are a single
pointer-events-transp

react` + the host services it declares. Decorations are a single
pointer-events-transparent overlay.
## Verification

- **Static audit** (`tools/audit-themes.mjs`, independent of the build): **159/159 checks
PASS**, 0

failures, 0 warnings — package shape, theme completeness, 127-token derivation per
theme, full WCAG

contrast matrix, effects-CSS discipline, built-bundle truth.
- **End-to-end verification** on a live

`dsh web` instance (`docs/qa/verification-report.md`):
**8/8 items PASS** — all three themes via th

e row and via persisted reload, live body tokens
byte-identical to the derived sets (127/127 × 3), p

ersistence with no palette flash, clean
exit path, effects switch (pixel-diff confined to the overla

y), menus/composer/settings
regressions clean, live contrast body 12.6–15.4:1 and composer 11.2–13.1

:1.
- Two LOW defects found by the verifier (boot-restore grace race when choosing a built-in
appear

ance within ~5 s of a reload; missing explicit `:focus-visible` ring on the row
controls) are fixed

and re-verified; details and evidence (28 screenshots, 57 reproducible
step scripts) are in `docs/qa

re-verified; details and evidence (28 screenshots, 57 reproducible
step scripts) are in `docs/qa/`.
